basis: Combined immunodeficiency and bronchiectasis define the syndrome; cancer predisposition does not establish additional organ damage.
Neuroendocrine neoplasm arising in autonomic paraganglia; secretion and metastases do not establish common additional organ damage.
Tumor arises in the jejunum; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Neonatal diabetes, congenital sensorineural deafness and cataracts are the three defining manifestations; additional findings vary.
Tumor of the reproductive collecting ducts of the rete testis; no endocrine tissue involvement is specified.
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%. Biliary atresia occurs in only 5-29%.
Umbrella for multiple endocrine gland tumors; other tumor sites vary across its constituent syndromes.
Peripheral nerve sheath tumor arising in the ureter; both neural origin and urinary location define the lesion.
Autoimmune glomerular inflammation in lupus; other systemic lupus manifestations are not intrinsic to this renal disease concept.
Renal tubular aldosterone resistance defines the electrolyte and acid-base disorder; associated urinary infection is a separate condition.
Craniosynostosis, ocular abnormalities and great-toe skeletal defects define this syndrome; no additional common organ damage is documented.
GM2 storage disorder with adult neurodegeneration and neuropathy; dysphagia and weakness reflect neurologic dysfunction, not separate organ injury.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across this variable chromosomal duplication; facial differences alone add no organ axis.
Defined by hereditary cutaneous melanoma and glioma susceptibility; these primary axes describe predisposition, not established tumors or damage.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorder affecting skin, hair and eyes; ocular hypopigmentation and nystagmus occur in 30-79%.
Developmental delay in 24/28 and intellectual disability in 18/28 define the disorder; joint hypermobility 8/28 and other organ lesions fall below 30%.
Chronic syphilitic meningoencephalitis directly destroys cerebral cortical parenchyma.
Systemic Salmonella Typhi infection with intestinal lymphoid invasion; rash and organ enlargement alone do not establish damage; encephalitis is 5-29%.
Intellectual disability and cortical malformation define the disorder; optic atrophy is reported in 1/3 patients, meeting 30% in a very small series.
Forebrain malformation defines disease; microphthalmia and unilateral cleft lip each occur in 2/4. Pituitary failure 1/8 is excluded; nasal shape alone adds no axis.
Viral hemorrhagic fever with prominent cytopenias; hepatitis affects >30% of symptomatic patients. Neurologic complications occur in a minority.
Embryopathy defined by microcephaly, intellectual disability and congenital heart defects; affected offspring do not themselves have phenylketonuria.
Sensory-autonomic neuropathy with developmental impairment; gastrointestinal dysmotility/reflux in 5/5. Central apnea is neurologic; infections are secondary.
Melanocytic neoplasm arising in skin; includes both cutaneous melanoma and benign melanocytic nevi.
Serous adenocarcinoma arising in a uterine ligament, a reproductive structure outside the organ axes.
